newsitem.title: CHINA: Survey says 78 pct China consumers cheated in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Survey says 78 pct China consumers cheated in 1996.

text.p: A national consumer survey has found that 78.4 percent of Chinese consumers were victims of some form of commercial fraud in 1996, the Market Daily said on Thursday.

The China Consumers' Association survey, based on 11,027 questionaires collected from 1,500 counties, found promotions such as direct sales, bargains or the promise of prizes for buyers were the most common cover for fraud, it said.
In the service sector, fraud was most prevalent among repairs of household appliances, restaurants and bars and medical services, the newspaper said.
The percentage of consumers reporting they had been cheated had risen BY 20 percentage points compared with 1995, but this did not mean the commercial fraud situation was deteriorating, it said.
Many consumers had previously been ignorant of their rights and had not even known that they way they were treated counted as commercial fraud, it said.
